intro: Kampala rewards visitors with lively markets, green hills and a buzzing food and music scene. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: No metro or tram; public transport is matatu minibuses, boda-bodas and special-hire taxis.
Matatus run fixed routes from the Old Taxi Park and other stages; fares are roughly UGX 1,000-3,000.
Boda-bodas are fast but risky; agree the fare first, usually UGX 3,000-20,000 in town.
Uber, Bolt, Faras and SafeBoda apps work in Kampala; app bodas include helmets.
Special-hire taxis rarely use meters; agree a fare, often UGX 15,000-20,000 for central trips.
Driving is possible but hectic; walking is fine by day in central areas, and there is no ferry service.

kasubi.name: Kasubi Tombs
kasubi.price_text: ≈ UGX 10,000–30,000 for foreign visitors; check on the day
kasubi.hours: Daily roughly 08:00–18:00; check on the day
kasubi.tip: This is the burial site of Buganda kings and a UNESCO site. Dress modestly and ask before taking photos.

gaddafi-mosque.name: Gaddafi National Mosque
gaddafi-mosque.price_text: ≈ UGX 5,000–20,000 for visitors; check on the day
gaddafi-mosque.hours: Daily, outside prayer times; check on the day
gaddafi-mosque.tip: Climb the minaret for one of the best views over Kampala. Women cover hair and shoulders.

namugongo.name: Namugongo Martyrs Shrine
namugongo.hours: Daily roughly 07:00–18:00; check on the day
namugongo.tip: A major pilgrimage site with striking modern architecture. It is far from the centre, so take a taxi.

bahai-temple.name: Baha'i House of Worship
bahai-temple.tip: Quiet gardens and a domed prayer hall open to all faiths. A calm break from the city.

independence-monument.name: Independence Monument, Uganda
independence-monument.tip: A quick photo stop in the centre. Combine it with a short walk around the nearby streets.

matooke.name: Matooke (steamed green banana)
matooke.price_text: ≈ UGX 8,000–25,000 per plate at local eateries
matooke.tip: Uganda's staple dish, served with groundnut sauce and meat or beans. Try it at a simple local restaurant.

national-museum.name: Uganda National Museum
national-museum.tip: Good introduction to Uganda's history and ethnography. Allow an hour or two.

owino-market.name: Owino Market
owino-market.price_text: Free to enter; bring small cash
owino-market.tip: Huge, busy second-hand and produce market. Keep valuables close and go with a local if you can.

nakasero-market.name: Nakasero Market
nakasero-market.tip: Central produce market for fruit, spices and local snacks. Good for photos and cheap eats.

kololo-view.name: Kololo Hill viewpoint
kololo-view.tip: One of the highest points in the city, with views over the seven hills. Go at sunset.

city-walk.name: Central Kampala heritage walk
city-walk.price_text: ≈ UGX 30,000–80,000 with a guide; check on the day
city-walk.tip: Walk between the monuments, markets and old buildings with a local guide. Ask your hotel to arrange one.

boda-tour.name: Boda boda city tour
boda-tour.price_text: ≈ UGX 40,000–100,000 per person; agree the price first
boda-tour.tip: Motorbike taxis are the fastest way around. Wear the helmet and agree the route and price before you start.

craft-market.name: National Theatre Craft Market
craft-market.tip: Souvenirs, carvings and textiles in one place. Bargain politely and start low.

ndere.name: Ndere Cultural Centre show
ndere.hours: Shows on some evenings; book ahead
ndere.tip: Traditional dance and music in an open-air theatre. Confirm the show day before you go.

lake-victoria-beach.name: Lake Victoria beach (Munyonyo side)
lake-victoria-beach.price_text: ≈ UGX 5,000–20,000 entry; check on the day
lake-victoria-beach.tip: Relaxed lakeside spots for fish and a drink. Water quality varies, so check before swimming.

bugolobi-food.name: Bugolobi food and cafe strip
bugolobi-food.tip: Easy area for a range of restaurants and cafes. Good for a relaxed dinner.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Markets, music, craft shops and the city's buzzing street life.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Rolex chapati rolls, luwombo and grilled tilapia by the lake.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Green hills, botanical gardens and a boat ride on Lake Victoria.

stays.why: Quiet, leafy hill close to the centre; many embassies, cafés and mid-range to upscale hotels.
Central and walkable to the market, shops and offices; good mix of budget and business hotels.
Relaxed suburb with a popular mall, restaurants and easy rides to the centre.
On Lake Victoria; resorts and lake views, but 20–40 minutes by car from the centre.

food: Start with a rolex: a chapati rolled with eggs and vegetables, a cheap street breakfast or lunch.
Try luwombo (meat or chicken steamed in banana leaves) and matoke at a local restaurant.
Eat grilled tilapia by Lake Victoria in Munyonyo or at lakeside spots; check the price per fish first.
For cheap eats, look for local cafeterias serving beans, rice and posho; a meal is often a few thousand UGX.
Drink bottled or filtered water, and be cautious with raw salads and street food if your stomach is sensitive.
more_time: Add a day for the Uganda Museum and the Kasubi Tombs area (check opening hours on the day).
Take a boat trip on Lake Victoria or visit the Uganda Wildlife Education Centre in Entebbe.
Shop for crafts and fabrics at the National Theatre craft market and Owino market with a local guide.
